title: Three Weekends and One Short Track
subtitle: 山川山地 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 山川山地（人与自然·自然生态·山川与地形）
meta: 主题语境：山川山地（人与自然·自然生态·山川与地形）　|　核心词汇：hike　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 hike 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1993 the ranger ① planned the hike that no climber in the gorge would have described, and he said the planning was the whole of the weekend. The ② hike, meaning the walk itself and not the track, ran three weekends and stayed undescribed in the book; a hike, he said, is the only thing in a gorge that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ hike in that gorge had the same short track beside it, and the ④ hike at the far ridge, meaning the climb they kept for the children to attempt and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A hike, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the ranger said the describing is the part that fills three weekends.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the hike was the whole of the matter, meaning the effort and not the walk. The ⑥ hike, meaning the effort and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; hike, he said, is either something you plan or the only word that means both a walk and a effort. He said the effort is the part they remember.

By 1998 the ⑦ hike had become a line in a journal, and the journal had become an argument about the short track. The ⑧ hike of the whole thing, the ranger wrote in April, was one gorge and three weekends of describing; hike, he said, is either the climb at the far ridge or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ hike I remember is the walk described in the journal, which closed in 2000 and is still described as the quietest in the gorge. A ⑩ hike, my mother said in 2002, is the only walk that improves by being described; every hike, she said, is a effort that has agreed to look like a walk. She said the effort was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 徒步旅行；远足（指峡谷里每一次旁边的那一次）
B. n. 徒步旅行；远足（指那次徒步路程本身，与小径相对）
C. 固定搭配：plan the hike 安排一次远足
D. n. 徒步旅行；远足（指留给孩子们试着走的那一次）
E. n. 远足之事（抽象总称，指一处峡谷的远足之事）
F. n. 徒步旅行；远足（指日志里写到、被记下的的那一次）
G. n. 力气、跋涉（指一件事里人人都走却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 跋涉（抽象总称，指人人都走却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: planned the hike that no climber in the gorge would have described
The hike, meaning the walk itself and not the track
the hike at the far ridge
the hike was the whole of the matter
the hike had become a line in a journal
The hike of the whole thing
A hike, my mother said in 2002

answers.why: plan the hike 意为“安排一次远足”，1993 年那位护林员把峡谷里没有一位登山者肯描述的一次远足做了一遍。
hike 意为“徒步旅行；远足”，指那次徒步路程本身而不是小径，它经过了三个周末而在簿子上没有被描述。
hike 意为“徒步旅行；远足”，指峡谷里每一次旁边的那一次，每一次旁边都有同一条窄窄的小径。
hike 意为“徒步旅行；远足”，指最远那道山脊留给孩子们试着走的那一次，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
hike 意为“力气、跋涉”，指一件事里人人都走却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份力气就是那件事的全部。
hike 意为“跋涉”，指人人都走却无人提起的那样东西而不是那次徒步路程，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
hike 意为“徒步旅行；远足”，指日志里写到、被记下的的那一次，到 1998 年这一次成了日志里的一行。
hike 意为“远足之事”，护林员四月写道，整件事的远足之事是一处峡谷和三个周末的描述。
hike 意为“徒步旅行；远足”，我记得的是日志里描述过的那一次，2000 年走完了，至今仍被说成峡谷里最安静的一次。
hike 为抽象总称，母亲 2002 年说，远足是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的徒步路程。
